lamp.source: Chakrabarty, Laban and Wu, 'Can AI writing be salvaged?', CHI 2025, arXiv 2409.14509 (CC BY 4.0), section 4.4. 'House rule' marks our own rules that LAMP does not cover.

note: Patina G1 tells. Rebuilt from the documented tells (anti-sameness guide v1.1, human-voice skill, Luke's r/WritingWithAI checklist and style sheet 5b, Nathan's ten rules, kitchen-table kill list, Wikipedia Signs of AI writing). Never paste this list into a drafting prompt (Antislop's pink elephant). Change only with a test and a CHANGELOG line.

families.afterthought-aside: A 1 to 4 word adverbial slipped in after a comma in narration (', once,', ', left side,', 'The remote, one hand.'). Fine once a page; as a habit it is a cadence (Nathan, 6 Nov 2026). Counted by form in fiction narration only.
families.em-dash: Em or en dash used as a dash. Nathan's house rule: none, ever.
families.not-x-but-y: Negative parallelism: 'it's not X, it's Y', 'not just X but Y', 'Y, not X.', 'They aren't X. They're Y.' The stickiest tell.
families.run-up: Staged run-up or rhetorical question answered at once ('The result?', 'Here's the thing').
families.ing-tail: '-ing' clause that comments on importance (', highlighting...', ', ensuring...').
families.copula-dodge: 'serves as', 'stands as', 'boasts' where 'is' or 'has' would do.
families.style-word: Excess-vocabulary words from tuned models (Kobak et al. 2025; Liang et al. 2024).
families.pet-word: Fiction pet words from r/WritingWithAI and Wikipedia's mid-2026 list; fine alone, a tell in bulk.
families.connector: Signposting connector opening a sentence (Additionally, Moreover).
families.the-way: 'The way' simile or 'with the X of someone who' (invents a third person to describe your character).
families.stage-direction: Mood stage direction on a dialogue tag ('he said, to the window').
families.body-emotion: Stock body-sensation emotion (chest tightened, knuckles white).
families.stock-beat: Stock beat: something shifted, the room fell silent, a breath she didn't know she was holding.
families.irony-tail: Trailing irony clause (', which was another way of saying...', ', which is worse').
families.landing: The landing verb: a modern motion idiom standing in for the plain act ('the strip she lands on'), often with a vague container noun and a narrator's 'happens to be' reveal. She is not an aeroplane.
families.landing-verb: Soft cousins of the landing verb (ends up, stumbles upon): fine once, a fingerprint in bulk.
families.product-subject: Headline where the product is the one acting ('Your website answers...'). Nathan judged every such line flat. The reader should hold the verb (Speak to People, 6 Nov 2026).
families.blame: Headline that casts the reader as failing ('Not answering your phone?', 'How many jobs went to...'). Scolding is not speaking to someone.
families.orphan: Short line that opens on It, This, That or They with nothing before it: a cold reader cannot tell what it is (Nathan: 'It didn't guess').
families.bare-negative: Short line that only says what did not happen. Say what it does.
families.faux-plain: A made-up customer explaining how the product works ('It knows because I...'). Real people say what happened to them.
families.design-leak: A word from the project's own design language in spoken or testimonial copy (Sheaf: 'papers'). Customers do not talk like the style sheet.
families.dropped-speaker: The speaker was cut ('Found my boiler warranty...'). Put the I back: Claim the Line (libraries/principles/claim-the-line.md).
families.metadiscourse: Empty signposting and recap closers ('In this section', 'The key takeaway'). Source pack 5 Nov 2026.
families.signpost: Narrator or writer signposting sincerity ('I'll say it plainly', 'I want to be clear').
families.drumroll-split: A caption split so the second line pays off the first ('Each sentence,' / 'checked.').
families.same-shape: Cards or lines that share one shape in a row.
families.budget: Line over the profile's word budget.
families.specificity: Too few checkable specifics (numbers, names, places, quotes).
families.rhythm: Sentence lengths too even (Nathan's rule 1: vary radically).
families.staccato: Three or more very short narration sentences in a row.
families.same-opening: Three sentences in a row that open with the same word.
families.corrective-framing: Mid-2026 corrective framing: should be treated as X rather than Y, does not establish that.
families.format: Assistant formatting habits: bold lead-ins on every list item, emoji bullets.
families.band: Nearly every sentence inside 8 to 20 words (Wikipedia, mid-2026 sign).

rules.hint: Use a full stop, comma, colon or brackets.

rules.re: \b(?:it|that|this|they|he|she|which)(?:'s|’s| is| was| are| were)?\s*(?:not|n't|n’t)\b[^.;:!?\n]{1,40}?[,;]\s*(?:it|that|this|they|he|she)(?:'s|’s| is| was|'re|’re| are| were)\b
rules.hint: Say Y. Drop the X it is 'not'.
Say the second thing on its own.
End on the thing it is. Cut ', not X'.
'They aren't X. They're Y.' Say Y.
'Not X. Not Y. Just Z.' Say Z.
Open on what it is, not what it is not.

rules.re: \b(?:The result|The best part|The catch|The twist|The kicker|The problem|The answer|The truth|The secret|Honestly|The good news|The bad news)\?
rules.hint: Cut the run-up; start with the answer.
Cut the announcement; say the thing.
A question answered at once is a drumroll. State the fact.
Keep the true one, or give four with an odd one.
Cut the tail; if it matters, give it its own plain sentence.

rules.re: \b(?:serves as|serve as|stands as|acts as a|boasts|boast a)\b
rules.hint: Use 'is' or 'has'.
Use the plain word a person would say.

rules.re: \b(?:the|today's|an ever-changing|a changing) (?:\w+ )?landscape of\b|\bnavigat(?:e|es|ing) the (?:complexities|world|challenges)\b|\bin the heart of\b|\brich (?:history|tapestry|heritage)\b
rules.hint: Name the actual place or thing.
Kitchen-table kill list word.
Fine once; in bulk it is a fingerprint. Swap or cut some.
Let the ideas join by their own logic (Nathan's rule 7).

rules.re: \b(?:I hope this (?:email |message )?finds you well|I'?m writing to|I am writing to|let'?s dive in|dive into|in today'?s (?:fast-paced|digital|modern) world|it'?s important to note|it is important to note|it'?s worth noting|it is worth noting|plays? a (?:crucial|vital|key|pivotal|significant) role|is a testament to|look no further|rest assured|don'?t hesitate to|I'?d be (?:happy|glad) to|great question|I hope this helps|let me know if you have any (?:other )?questions|in conclusion|at the end of the day|when it comes to|whether you'?re a|to the next level|imagine a world|in a world where|the power of|stands the test of time)\b
rules.hint: Stock phrase. Say the specific thing, or cut.

rules.re: \b(?:thrilled|absolutely|I completely understand|I totally understand|so excited|we'?re excited|delighted to|amazing|awesome|don'?t worry|no worries at all)\b
rules.hint: One real kind line beats three warm words.
One caveat, said once.
Say what happened.
Swap for a simile from the narrator's own world, or cut. Watch the dose.

rules.re: \bwith the \w+ of (?:someone|somebody|a man|a woman|a person|one) who\b
rules.hint: Describe this character directly.
Luke A12: no mood stage directions. Give the line plain, or an action beat.
Sometimes just name the feeling, or show it by an act.

rules.re: \bsomething (?:shifted|changed|broke|cracked|flickered) (?:in|inside|behind|across)\b|\b(?:room|world|house|kitchen|car|table) (?:fell|went) (?:silent|quiet|still)\b|\bbreath (?:he|she|I|they) didn'?t know\b|\blet out a breath\b|\ba beat passed\b
rules.hint: Name the actual movement or sound.

rules.re: \b(?:like|as if|as though) (?:it|that|this)(?:'s|’s| is| was| were) (?:a|an|the|some) [^.;:!?\n]{1,30}? (?:he|she|they|I|we|you)(?:'s|’s|'d|’d|'ve|’ve| has| had| have) been \w+ing\b
rules.hint: Mind-reading simile: the narrator explains a minor character's inner life. Show the act, or cut the simile.
Fine once, can be the best laugh; in bulk the narrator is reading minds.
Say the plain act: she gleans in, walks into, works, finds herself in. She is not an aeroplane.
Narrator's wink built on a landing verb. Keep the irony if it is the point, but say it plainly ('As it happens, the field she gleans is Boaz's').
Fine once; in bulk say what they did.
Make the reader the one who acts: what do THEY get to do? ("Keep your Saturday.")

rules.re: ^\s*(?:Not \w+ing\b|Stop \w+ing\b|Still \w+ing\b|Are you still\b|Why (?:aren't|aren’t|don't|don’t) you\b|How many \w+ (?:went|did you lose|have you lost)\b)
rules.hint: Do not cast the reader as failing. Offer what they keep or gain.
Name the thing. A stranger reading only this line must know what it is about. A dummy it ('It's good to talk') is fine.
Say what happened to the speaker, not how the product works.
Put the speaker back ("I found..."), and one small proud beat. Advisory until H1 is measured.

rules.re: \b(?:[Tt]he key takeaway|[Tt]he bottom line is|[Ii]n this (?:section|article|post|guide|video)|[Aa]s we(?:'ve|’ve| have) seen|[Ll]et(?:'s|’s| us) (?:dive in|dive into|take a (?:closer )?look|explore)|[Ii]n the (?:next|following) section|[Tt]o sum (?:it )?up|[Aa]ll in all|[Aa]t the end of the day)\b
rules.hint: Cut the signpost or the recap; say the thing.

rules.re: ,\s*which (?:was|is) (?:another way of saying|worse|better|the point|saying something|to say)\b
rules.hint: Keep only if it holds a fact.

rules.re: \b(?:I'?ll say it plainly|I want to be clear|let me be clear|I'?ll be honest|to be honest|make no mistake|I'?ll say now)\b
rules.hint: Cut the announcement of sincerity; the plain line is enough.
Stock AI name; pick one from the setting.

rules.re: \b(?:should|must|can|is best) (?:be )?(?:treated|seen|understood|read|framed) as [^.;\n]{1,50}?\brather than\b|\bshould not be confused with\b|\bdoes not (?:establish|imply|entail) that\b
rules.hint: Mid-2026 corrective framing (Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing). Say what it is.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing, 2 Nov 2026

rules.hint: Bold label at the start of every list item reads as a template (Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing). Use plain sentences or a table.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing, 2 Nov 2026

rules.hint: Emoji opening a list item: an assistant habit.
rules.source: Wikipedia, Signs of AI writing, 2 Nov 2026

rules.hint: Kitchen-table: no exclamation marks.

fiction.note: Doses are per 1,000 words. Also run luke tools/readability_lint.py. cvFloor 0.45, not Luke's 0.55: Cather (1918, human) measures 0.47 (post-hoc change, 2 Nov 2026).

captions.note: One card per line of input; ' / ' splits the on-screen lines of a card.

email.note: Email or message sent as Nathan (voice nathan-plain).

pro-email.note: Professional email from a business or an agent, not as Nathan: replies to clients, quotes, chasers, Upwork messages. Voice: kitchen-table, or nathan-plain when signed by Nathan.

technical.note: Industrial, technical and B2B text: specs, help docs, method statements, reports. Even sentence lengths are normal here, so the rhythm floor is low; vagueness is not.

playful.note: Playful copy: social posts, packaging, fun product moments, storytelling ads. Exclamation marks and questions are allowed; AI-style threes and fake warmth are not. Voice: storyteller.

headline.note: Taglines, hero lines, page titles, title cards, ad headlines. One line per unit; ' / ' adds a subline. Write a brief first (templates/headline-brief.txt) and run 'patina lines'.

testimonial.note: A customer or owner speaking, one quote per line. Claim the Line: keep the I and one proud beat.

spoken.note: Voiceover and narration written to be heard. Short spoken lines run even, so the rhythm floor is 0.3. Read it aloud (G5).

ui.note: One string per line. Prefix a line with 'title:', 'button:', 'help:' or 'error:' to apply the kitchen-table budget (8, 3, 20 words, 2 sentences).
